 91 /// Returns the bitwidth of the given scalar or pointer type. For vector types,
 92 /// returns the element type's bitwidth.
 93 static unsigned getBitWidth(Type *Ty, const DataLayout &DL) {

100 // Given the provided Value and, potentially, a context instruction, return
101 // the preferred context instruction (if any).
102 static const Instruction *safeCxtI(const Value *V, const Instruction *CxtI) {
103   // If we've been provided with a context instruction, then use that (provided
104   // it has been inserted).
105   if (CxtI && CxtI->getParent())
106     return CxtI;
107 
108   // If the value is really an already-inserted instruction, then use that.
109   CxtI = dyn_cast<Instruction>(V);
110   if (CxtI && CxtI->getParent())
111     return CxtI;
112 
113   return nullptr;
114 }

153 void llvm::computeKnownBits(const Value *V, KnownBits &Known, unsigned Depth,
154                             const SimplifyQuery &Q) {
155   // Since the number of lanes in a scalable vector is unknown at compile time,
156   // we track one bit which is implicitly broadcast to all lanes.  This means
157   // that all lanes in a scalable vector are considered demanded.
158   auto *FVTy = dyn_cast<FixedVectorType>(V->getType());
159   APInt DemandedElts =
160       FVTy ? APInt::getAllOnes(FVTy->getNumElements()) : APInt(1, 1);
161   ::computeKnownBits(V, DemandedElts, Known, Depth, Q);
162 }

190 static bool haveNoCommonBitsSetSpecialCases(const Value *LHS, const Value *RHS,
191                                             const SimplifyQuery &SQ) {
192   // Look for an inverted mask: (X & ~M) op (Y & M).
193   {
194     Value *M;
195     if (match(LHS, m_c_And(m_Not(m_Value(M)), m_Value())) &&
196         match(RHS, m_c_And(m_Specific(M), m_Value())) &&
197         isGuaranteedNotToBeUndef(M, SQ.AC, SQ.CxtI, SQ.DT))
198       return true;
199   }
200 
201   // X op (Y & ~X)
202   if (match(RHS, m_c_And(m_Not(m_Specific(LHS)), m_Value())) &&
203       isGuaranteedNotToBeUndef(LHS, SQ.AC, SQ.CxtI, SQ.DT))
204     return true;
205 
206   // X op ((X & Y) ^ Y) -- this is the canonical form of the previous pattern
207   // for constant Y.
208   Value *Y;
209   if (match(RHS,
210             m_c_Xor(m_c_And(m_Specific(LHS), m_Value(Y)), m_Deferred(Y))) &&
211       isGuaranteedNotToBeUndef(LHS, SQ.AC, SQ.CxtI, SQ.DT) &&
212       isGuaranteedNotToBeUndef(Y, SQ.AC, SQ.CxtI, SQ.DT))
213     return true;
214 
215   // Peek through extends to find a 'not' of the other side:
216   // (ext Y) op ext(~Y)
217   if (match(LHS, m_ZExtOrSExt(m_Value(Y))) &&
218       match(RHS, m_ZExtOrSExt(m_Not(m_Specific(Y)))) &&
219       isGuaranteedNotToBeUndef(Y, SQ.AC, SQ.CxtI, SQ.DT))
220     return true;
221 
222   // Look for: (A & B) op ~(A | B)
223   {
224     Value *A, *B;
225     if (match(LHS, m_And(m_Value(A), m_Value(B))) &&
226         match(RHS, m_Not(m_c_Or(m_Specific(A), m_Specific(B)))) &&
227         isGuaranteedNotToBeUndef(A, SQ.AC, SQ.CxtI, SQ.DT) &&
228         isGuaranteedNotToBeUndef(B, SQ.AC, SQ.CxtI, SQ.DT))
229       return true;
230   }
231 
232   // Look for: (X << V) op (Y >> (BitWidth - V))
233   // or        (X >> V) op (Y << (BitWidth - V))
234   {
235     const Value *V;
236     const APInt *R;
237     if (((match(RHS, m_Shl(m_Value(), m_Sub(m_APInt(R), m_Value(V)))) &&
238           match(LHS, m_LShr(m_Value(), m_Specific(V)))) ||
239          (match(RHS, m_LShr(m_Value(), m_Sub(m_APInt(R), m_Value(V)))) &&
240           match(LHS, m_Shl(m_Value(), m_Specific(V))))) &&
241         R->uge(LHS->getType()->getScalarSizeInBits()))
242       return true;
243   }
244 
245   return false;
246 }

{"test":["```llvm
; Test case demonstrating the bug in breakSelfRecursivePHI
; The bug is that CtxIOut is not updated when handling select instructions,
; but is updated when handling 2-operand PHI nodes. This inconsistency
; could lead to wrong analysis results.

define i32 @test_bug(i1 %cond, i32 %x) {
entry:
  ; Create a value with context-dependent known bits
  %x.addr = add i32 %x, 1
  br label %loop

loop:
  %phi = phi i32 [ 0, %entry ], [ %sel, %loop ]
  ; Select where one arm is the phi (recursive)
  %sel = select i1 %cond, i32 %phi, i32 %x.addr
  br label %loop
}

; When computeKnownBits analyzes %phi:
; 1. It looks at incoming value %sel
; 2. %sel is select i1 %cond, i32 %phi, i32 %x.addr
; 3. breakSelfRecursivePHI identifies this as a recursive select
; 4. It sets ValOut = %x.addr (the other arm)
; 5. But it does NOT update CtxIOut (bug!)
; 6. CtxIOut remains set to the terminator of the incoming block
; 7. When computeKnownBits analyzes %x.addr with wrong context,
;    it might get wrong results if %x.addr's known bits depend on context
```","opt -S -passes=instcombine -o /dev/null"],"thoughts":"Bug Triggering Analysis:
The patch introduces a new function `breakSelfRecursivePHI` to handle recursive select/PHI patterns in `computeKnownBits` and `computeKnownFPClass`. However, there are two critical bugs in this function:

1. **Uninitialized CtxIOut**: When `ValOut == PHI` (direct self-reference), the function returns without setting `CtxIOut`, leaving it uninitialized. While the caller skips this case (`if (IncValue == P) continue`), leaving a reference parameter uninitialized is undefined behavior and poor practice.

2. **Inconsistent context handling**: The function handles select instructions and 2-operand PHI nodes differently:
   - For select instructions (lines 605-607): Sets `ValOut = V` but does NOT update `CtxIOut`
   - For 2-operand PHI nodes (lines 613-622): Sets `ValOut = IncPhi->getIncomingValue(1 - Idx)` AND updates `CtxIOut = IncPhi->getIncomingBlock(1 - Idx)->getTerminator()`

This inconsistency is a bug because when analyzing the other arm of a select (`V`), we should use the select instruction itself as the context, not the terminator of the incoming block. The context instruction matters for assumptions and other context-sensitive analysis. Using the wrong context could lead to incorrect known bits computation.

The bug manifests when:
- A PHI node has a select instruction as an incoming value
- The select contains the PHI as one arm (creating recursion)
- The other arm (`V`) has known bits that depend on context (e.g., based on assumptions)
- The wrong context instruction leads to incorrect known bits computation

Fix Weakness Analysis:
The fix should:
1. Always initialize `CtxIOut` in `breakSelfRecursivePHI`, even when `ValOut == PHI`
2. Update `CtxIOut` when handling select instructions, setting it to the select instruction itself (not the terminator of the incoming block)
3. The comment on lines 609-610 ("Same for select") is misleading since the code is in an `else if` block and doesn't handle select instructions the same way

The patch's weakness is that it introduces inconsistent handling of similar patterns (select vs. PHI), which violates the principle of least surprise and could lead to subtle miscompilations."}
